problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}?$

$$
U={[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

- $U={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$
- $V={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}$
- $W={[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
${{u}_{1},{u}_{2}},$
${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}},$ and 
${{w}_{1},{w}_{2}}$, respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=0+0=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=1+0=1 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=0+1=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $V,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0+0=0\ne 1 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthonormal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is not an orthonormal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ only".
